safety_lead_time.comparison_action: Reduce safety lead time from 3.0 to 2 days

narrative: Material PL1__MAAD5FC2 exhibits erratic demand (CV=0.38, right-skewed) with no statistically significant trend over the 130-day observation window. Lead times are highly volatile (CV=0.90), with occasional spikes to 4 working days, which dominates the safety stock calculation. The (r,Q) continuous review policy is selected because demand is non-intermittent and the MOQ of 1,751 units is naturally accommodated by the EOQ of 2,803 units. Raising safety stock from 540 to 871 units is necessary to close the service level gap attributable to lead time volatility.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is erratic but fully continuous (zero-demand days = 0%), making continuous review more efficient than periodic. EOQ exceeds MOQ, so no MOQ-driven distortion. The (r,Q) model with a fixed reorder point and fixed order quantity is the appropriate choice for this demand-and-lead-time profile.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Capacity utilization is 43.7% (3,675 / 8,404 units). The capacity constraint does not bind; no service or cost degradation from storage limits.
